allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

statement_nl: Let n>1. If b_1,...,b_{n-1} are nonnegative real numbers, and u_1,...,u_{n-1} is a nonincreasing reordering of the same multiset of numbers, then sum_{k=1}^{n-1} b_k/k <= sum_{k=1}^{n-1} u_k/k. If equality holds, then the original list b_1,...,b_{n-1} is already nonincreasing.
